# opencode-usage-bar [OpenCode Go](https://opencode.ai/docs/go/) usage bars for the [opencode](https://opencode.ai) v2 TUI - a persistent bar next to the prompt in sessions, plus a `/limit` popup with all three windows. Read-only; talks directly to the official usage API, never sends LLM prompts.


> [!IMPORTANT] > For opencode **1.x**, visit the [`OpenCode-v1` branch](https://github.com/Leogimp/opencode-usage-bar/tree/OpenCode-v1) - the last version built for the V1 TUI plugin API. ## Install ```sh opencode plugin add "@leo.gimp/opencode-usage-bar" ``` That installs the package and adds it to `~/.config/opencode/cli.json` (the V2 terminal settings file). Quit and restart opencode afterwards - CLI plugin config is read at startup. Requires opencode **v2**. For opencode 1.x, use the [`OpenCode-v1` branch](https://github.com/Leogimp/opencode-usage-bar/tree/OpenCode-v1). To uninstall: ```sh opencode plugin remove "@leo.gimp/opencode-usage-bar" ``` ### Installing from a local checkout If you prefer running straight from a clone, `npm run install-plugin` copies the sources to `~/.config/opencode/usage-bar/` and adds that path to `cli.json`: ```sh npm install npm run install-plugin ``` This is an explicit opt-in step, never an automatic one. Useful flags: `--dry-run` to preview every change, `--no-config` to copy the files without touching `cli.json`, `--config-dir DIR` to target a different opencode config directory. Any config file it changes is backed up alongside as `.opencode-usage-bar.bak`, and it refuses to rewrite a config it cannot parse. The renderer libraries (`solid-js`, `@opentui/core`, `@opentui/solid`) are peer dependencies supplied by the opencode host, so neither install path copies them. A second copy would break rendering: OpenTUI's reconciler keys off module identity, so JSX compiled against a different copy than the one rendering it produces nothing at all. ## Features ### Session usage bar A full usage bar rendered on the right side of the prompt hint row (the same row as `agent · model · provider · effort`), inside active sessions: - Percent used, one decimal (`xx.x%`), 20-character `▓/░` bar, reset countdown (`4h 10m`, `3d 4h`, …) - Refreshes automatically every **60 seconds** (with in-flight request deduplication and a 60s response cache) - **Adaptive sizing** - mirrors opencode's own session layout (sidebar width, prompt padding) and terminal size, re-evaluated live on window resize: | Space available | Display | |---|---| | Plenty | full bar + percent + reset timer | | Tight | compact form `5h ▓▓░░░░░░ 11.0%` (no timer) | | Not enough | hidden - it never wraps or overlaps the prompt hints | - Only shown once you are inside a session, not on the home or fresh-session screen - Shows a dimmed `5h (unavailable)` if the request fails instead of silently disappearing ![session usage bar](assets/session-bar.png) ### `/limit` popup Type `/limit` (or `ctrl+p` → *Usage limits*) for a popup with all three OpenCode Go windows - rolling 5h, weekly, and monthly - each with a bar, percent used, and reset timer: - Fetches **fresh** data every time it opens (bypasses the 60s cache) - Reset timers keep ticking while the popup is open (30s tick) - Hosted dialog panel, centered over the session; close with `esc` - Footer shows the last four characters of the API key in use (`····xxxx`), so you can tell which account is displayed when several are connected - `[ hide usage bar ]` toggle below the windows - hides or shows the session prompt bar, persisted across restarts in plugin storage (a pre-V2 `~/.config/opencode/usage-bar.json` preference is migrated automatically on first run) ![/limit popup](assets/limit-popup.png) ### Data source Reads the official OpenCode Go quota endpoint: ``` GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage Authorization: Bearer ``` returning the rolling (5h), weekly, and monthly windows with percent used and reset times. The plugin is read-only - it never sends prompts, session data, or anything else to the LLM. ## Options Passed as the `options` object of the plugin entry in `cli.json`: | Option | Default | Description | |---|---|---| | `left_reserve` | `44` | Columns reserved for the left prompt hints. Increase if the bar hides too late. | | `sidebar_width` | `42` | Columns reserved for the session sidebar. Set `0` if you keep it hidden (e.g. `session.sidebar: "hide"` in `cli.json`). | | `padding` | `6` | Prompt box inner padding subtracted from the available width. | ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/v2/cli.json", "plugins": [ { "package": "@leo.gimp/opencode-usage-bar", "options": { "left_reserve": 60 } } ] } ``` ## Notes - Without an OpenCode Go key the plugin shows no bar - only the `/limit` command stays registered as a no-op. - Key resolution (first match wins): `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` env → the **active** OpenCode Go credential in opencode's credential store (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`) → the legacy `opencode-go` entry in `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json`. When several accounts are connected, the account actually in use is followed: switching accounts (`/connect`, credential activation) re-resolves the key via `credential.switched` events and refreshes usage immediately - no restart needed. - The package ships its TypeScript sources unbuilt, which is the documented shape for an opencode CLI plugin: the Bun host transpiles them on load. There is no `dist/` and no build step. ## Local development There is no build step - edit `src/` and restart opencode. To run from a checkout, point opencode at it directly in `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`: ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/v2/cli.json", "plugins": ["C:\\path\\to\\opencode-usage-bar"] } ``` The host transpiles the TypeScript on load, so a reload picks up source edits without any build step in between. ## Requirements - opencode **v2** (uses the V2 CLI plugin slot API, `@opencode/plugin/tui`). Not compatible with opencode 1.x. - An OpenCode Go subscription ## License MIT
